images.title: Drop a digit, every copy fills
images.purpose: Shows the digit puzzle solver in its simplest state: A is set to 2 in both places in AB + 37 = 6A, and a digit is dragged onto B.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. One column addition in large boxes across the centre, with one digit tile being dragged in.
images.exact_structure: A column addition: top row two boxes, the first filled teal (#0072B2) holding 2 and the second empty with a dashed outline holding B; second row a plus sign, then 3 and 7; a rule; answer row 6 and then a box filled teal (#0072B2) holding 2. A small amber (#E69F00) label carry 1 sits above the tens column. Below right, one reddish purple (#CC79A7) tile holding 5 with a curved dark arrow from it to the empty B box. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Setting A to 2 fills both copies of A; B must be 5 so that 25 + 37 = 62.
